title: Frida Kahlo: Pain into Art
description: Pain, resilience, and color—the life of a revolutionary Mexican artist.

questions.question: Which Mexican painter showed herself twice, hearts exposed and joined by a single artery, in a famous 1939 canvas?
questions.explanation: That's 'The Two Fridas,' painted the year she and Diego Rivera divorced. She said the Tehuana Frida is the one he loved; the European one, he didn't. They remarried in 1940.

questions.question: At what age did Frida Kahlo contract polio?
questions.explanation: It left her right leg thin, and kids yelled "Frida, pata de palo!" (peg leg). She hid it under extra socks, later long skirts. Some biographers suspect spina bifida instead.

questions.question: Polio was only the start—at 18, what kind of crash changed Kahlo's life forever?
questions.explanation: On Sept. 17, 1925, a streetcar smashed her bus. Her boyfriend recalled a passenger's gold powder spilling over her bleeding body, and onlookers crying "La bailarina!"

questions.question: What metal object pierced through Frida's pelvis in that bus accident?
questions.explanation: "The handrail pierced me the way a sword pierces a bull," she said. Bedridden for months, she began painting, with a special easel and a mirror fixed above her bed.

questions.question: Years of surgeries after the handrail injury, how did Kahlo arrive at her only solo show in Mexico, in April 1953?
questions.explanation: Doctors told her to stay home. Instead she greeted guests from her own four-poster bed, moved into the gallery. Months later her right leg was amputated: "Feet, what do I need you for when I have wings to fly?"
